stories.title: Facing US export controls, China's DeepSeek plans to make its own chips
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: China's DeepSeek is planning to develop its own semiconductor chips.
This initiative is a direct response to increasing US export controls.
The goal is to significantly reduce reliance on foreign suppliers like Nvidia and Huawei.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the active LLM development ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML topics including transformers and text-generation.
The mention of 'safetensors' indicates relevance to modern, efficient model deployment.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function in language tasks.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes standard ML frameworks (transformers, safetensors).
References an associated arXiv paper (arxiv:2606.19348), indicating recent academic research.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when running through Ollama 0.31.
The speedup is achieved via Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging the MLX framework.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster specifically when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in its MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these AI agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, has integrated MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview release, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command to simplify the setup and execution of coding tools.
It enables running various coding models (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex) both locally and in the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: How AI could enable autonomous robot workers in workplaces—and maybe homes
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The article discusses the evolution of robot autonomy driven by advancements in AI.
It explores the potential for these autonomous robots to be deployed in professional workplaces.
The technology also suggests future applications in domestic or home environments.

stories.title: From Fixed to Free Cameras: Calibration-Free View-Robust Vision-Language-Action Model
stories.author: Ran Xu
bullet_points: Addresses a critical real-world limitation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: fragility when camera setups change.
Proposes a novel approach where the model learns to be view-robust without requiring explicit camera extrinsic information.
This advancement significantly improves the deployability and practicality of VLA policies in dynamic robotic environments.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
stories.author: Azalia Mirhoseini
bullet_points: Introduces 'verification' as a new scaling axis for improving LLM capabilities, alongside traditional compute scaling.
Presents 'LLM-as-a-Verifier,' a general-purpose framework designed to check the correctness of LLM outputs.
The framework provides fine-grained feedback for agentic tasks without necessitating additional model training.

stories.title: Search Beyond What Can Be Taught: Evolving the Knowledge Boundary in Agentic Visual Generation
stories.author: Cong Wei
bullet_points: Addresses the 'world-knowledge bottleneck' in visual AI generators, where models fabricate information outside their training data.
Introduces SearchGen-20K and SearchGen-Bench, new benchmarks designed to test AI capabilities against unbounded, long-tailed user requests.
Focuses on evolving the knowledge boundary of agentic visual generation to handle novel, post-cutoff, and trending concepts.

stories.title: SPEARBench: A Benchmark for Naturalness Evaluation in Streaming Speech-to-Speech Language Models
stories.author: Laureano Moro-Velazquez
bullet_points: Introduces SPEARBench, a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating the naturalness of streaming speech-to-speech language models.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks by focusing on conversational nuances like timing, prosody, turn-taking, and interpersonal stance, which standard tests miss.
The benchmark aims to improve the perceived quality of direct spoken query answering systems by assessing holistic conversational behavior.

stories.title: From Fixed to Free Cameras: Calibration-Free View-Robust Vision-Language-Action Model
stories.author: Ran Xu
bullet_points: Addresses a critical real-world limitation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: fragility when camera setups change.
Proposes a novel approach where the VLA policy learns to be view-robust without requiring explicit camera extrinsic parameters.
Signifies a step toward more practical and deployable robotics systems that can handle dynamic environmental changes.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
stories.author: Azalia Mirhoseini
bullet_points: Introduces 'verification' as a new scaling axis for improving Large Language Model (LLM) capabilities, moving beyond just compute scaling.
Presents 'LLM-as-a-Verifier,' a general-purpose framework designed to check the correctness of LLM outputs.
The framework offers fine-grained feedback for agentic tasks without necessitating additional model training.

stories.title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Yuxiao Dong
bullet_points: Addresses the critical limitation of finite context windows in long-horizon agentic LLMs.
Proposes CompactionRL, a novel reinforcement learning strategy to handle extended interaction trajectories.
Utilizes context compaction to summarize past states, allowing agents to operate beyond maximum context limits.

stories.title: Faithfulness to Refusal: A Causal Audit of Neuron Selectors
stories.author: Vinay Kumar Sankarapu
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap between attribution scores (identifying important neurons) and actual causal importance in large language models.
The study uses paired audits based on one-shot neuron-row zeroing to test causal faithfulness of neuron selectors.
Attribution methods are shown to significantly outperform simpler activation and magnitude-based baselines in identifying dispensable model rows.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
stories.author: Azalia Mirhoseini
bullet_points: Introduces 'verification' as a new, critical scaling axis for Large Language Models (LLMs).
Presents 'LLM-as-a-Verifier,' a general-purpose framework for determining solution correctness.
The framework provides fine-grained feedback for agentic tasks without needing additional model training.

stories.title: The best AI models cite retracted papers, and they cannot know it
stories.author: mikeeus
bullet_points: Frontier AI models are confidently citing retracted scientific papers from their training data.
The models are unable to distinguish between cited and retracted works, even flagging older retractions.
The proposed solution requires external registry lookups, indicating a fundamental limitation in current model architectures.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Anthropic is launching Claude Cowork on mobile and web
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Anthropic's Claude Cowork AI platform is expanding its accessibility to mobile and web.
Initial rollout is restricted to Claude Max subscribers, with wider availability coming later.
This marks a shift from the platform's previous limitation to desktop-only access.

stories.title: Doom developer id reportedly cut in half as part of Xbox layoffs
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: id Software, a developer of Doom, has reportedly undergone significant layoffs.
The layoffs are linked to broader mass layoffs affecting Xbox.
Reports suggest around 50% of id Software's staff were cut, impacting departments like QA.

stories.title: This race car is made from plant fibers, volcanoes, ... and seawater?
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: A new race car, the T70S, is being constructed using unconventional, sustainable materials.
The vehicle incorporates plant fibers, volcanic materials, and seawater in its composition.
The T70S is designed with dual functionality, suitable for both racing competitions and road use.

stories.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Hao Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) when training large language models.
Proposes a 'weak-to-strong' distillation method: training RL on a smaller, cheaper model first.
The learned knowledge from the smaller model is then reused to improve a larger, stronger target model.

stories.title: Interpretable Human-Label-Free Deep Learning for Real-Bogus Classification with Uncertainty Quantification
stories.author: Vincenzo Piuri
bullet_points: Proposes a deep learning framework for Real-Bogus classification in transient surveys, addressing the high cost and noise of human labeling.
The model is designed to be trained without explicit human-labeled data, utilizing injected transients and bogus-dominated survey data.
Key features include robustness against strong class contamination and the provision of calibrated uncertainty quantification.

stories.title: Cortex: A Bidirectionally Aligned Embodied Agent Framework for Long-horizon Manipulation
stories.author: Tai Wang
bullet_points: Cortex is a new framework designed to improve embodied agents for long-horizon manipulation tasks.
It addresses the limitations of current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, which struggle due to their Markovian nature.
The framework features a bidirectional alignment and customized planning interface to bridge high-level planning and low-level execution.

stories.title: REDDIT: Correcting Model-Generated Timestamp Drift in ASR without Forgetting via Replay-Based Distribution Editing
stories.author: Hung-yi Lee
bullet_points: Addresses a technical flaw in modern autoregressive Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems where generated timestamps can drift over long non-speech segments.
Proposes a solution using 'Replay-Based Distribution Editing' to correct this timestamp drift without degrading the model's overall performance (catastrophic forgetting).
The research introduces specialized benchmarks (gap and long-gap) to rigorously test timestamp generation across various ASR models.

stories.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Hao Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) when applied to large language models.
Proposes a 'weak-to-strong' distillation method: training RL on a smaller, cheaper model first.
The learned knowledge from the smaller model is then reused to improve a larger, stronger target model.

stories.title: TabPack: Efficient Hyperparameter Ensembles for Tabular Deep Learning
stories.author: Artem Babenko
bullet_points: Introduces TabPack, a new efficient ensemble method for deep learning on tabular data.
Addresses the limitation of existing ensembles which use uniform hyperparameters, requiring extensive tuning.
Claims TabPack offers strong out-of-the-box performance with reduced dependency on traditional hyperparameter tuning.

stories.title: Fitted Occupancy-Ratio Evaluation without Bellman Completeness
stories.author: Nathan Kallus
bullet_points: The paper introduces Fitted Occupancy-Ratio Evaluation (FORE) for offline reinforcement learning.
FORE addresses limitations in existing methods by using a fitted fixed-point method based on an adjoint Bellman recursion.
The technique aims to characterize discounted occupancy ratios without requiring Bellman completeness, improving off-policy evaluation.

stories.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Hao Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of using Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) on large language models.
Proposes a 'weak-to-strong' distillation method: training RL on a smaller, cheaper model first.
The learned knowledge from the smaller model is then reused to improve a larger, stronger target model.

stories.title: SPEARBench: A Benchmark for Naturalness Evaluation in Streaming Speech-to-Speech Language Models
stories.author: Laureano Moro-Velazquez
bullet_points: SPEARBench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate the naturalness of streaming speech-to-speech language models.
It addresses a gap in current benchmarks by considering complex conversational factors like timing, prosody, and turn-taking.
The benchmark focuses on how jointly shaped elements influence the perceived quality of direct spoken responses.

stories.title: REDDIT: Correcting Model-Generated Timestamp Drift in ASR without Forgetting via Replay-Based Distribution Editing
stories.author: Hung-yi Lee
bullet_points: Addresses a critical issue in modern ASR systems where model-generated timestamps drift over long non-speech audio spans.
Proposes a novel solution using 'Replay-Based Distribution Editing' to correct this timestamp drift without degrading transcription accuracy.
Evaluates the method across 15 different timestamp-producing ASR models using custom gap and long-gap benchmarks.

stories.title: Faithfulness to Refusal: A Causal Audit of Neuron Selectors
stories.author: Vinay Kumar Sankarapu
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap between attribution scores (which suggest importance) and actual causal importance of neurons in language models.
The study employs a 'one-shot neuron-row zeroing' technique to perform paired causal audits.
Attribution methods are shown to significantly outperform simpler activation and magnitude-based baselines in identifying dispensable model rows.

stories.title: Selective Disclosure Watermarking for Large Language Models
stories.author: Qi Long
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in current LLM watermarking: the lack of selective disclosure.
Existing multi-bit watermarking schemes require revealing the entire embedded message to verify any part of the watermark.
The proposed work aims to enable controlled verification of specific segments of the watermark, reducing unnecessary information exposure.

stories.title: How Much is Left? LLMs Linearly Encode Their Remaining Output Length
stories.author: Adam Oberman
bullet_points: The research investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) possess an internal estimation of their remaining output length.
The study uses minimal-capacity linear probes on frozen hidden states of 7-8B open-weight models.
Findings suggest that LLM response structures (e.g., step-by-step solutions, retrievals) exhibit predictable and measurable length patterns.

stories.title: AI Wrote a Thread-Safe Counter. The CPU Made It 5x Slower.
stories.author: mrviduus
bullet_points: The article explores the performance implications of AI-generated code for a simple concurrent task (thread-safe counter).
It introduces the concept of the 'cache line' as a key factor in CPU performance bottlenecks.
The core finding is that the CPU hardware limitations significantly slowed down the AI-generated solution.

stories.title: Observability Design for the AI Era — Application / Infrastructure / CI / LLM, Each in Its Own Shape (Part 1)
stories.author: ryantsuji
bullet_points: The article discusses the necessity of reshaping observability data structures to accommodate the demands of the AI era.
It analyzes four distinct axes of observability—Application, Infrastructure, CI, and LLM—each requiring a unique design approach.
Key design decisions highlighted include client-side Gemini cost computation and routing LLM tracing data (e.g., Claude Code OTel) directly to BigQuery.

stories.title: Stop Thinking of LLMs as AI Models. Start Thinking of Them as Distributed Systems.
stories.author: vibudhsharma24
bullet_points: The article advocates for reframing Large Language Models (LLMs) from being viewed purely as AI models.
The author suggests treating LLMs instead as complex, distributed systems for better architectural understanding.
The discussion is grounded in practical experience shipping a 'production-ready' AI application.
